about.title: Manteca Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death in Manteca comes suddenly, the paperwork arrives before the grief has room to settle. In 2025, public records show 283 injury collisions in the city, 411 people hurt, and 2 lives lost on local roads, with reported crashes clustering on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. along corridors like SR-120, Yosemite Avenue, SR-99 and Main Street. California gives a spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain dependents and heirs able to step in when no one in that group exists. The claim is civil and moves separately from any criminal case tied to the same event. Families generally have two years from the date of death to file, and far less time when a public agency may share responsibility. We handle wrongful death claims on a contingency basis—no fee unless you recover.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. We can quickly confirm where your family fits before anything else is decided.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window shrinks sharply when a city, county or state agency may be involved. Reaching out now protects that timeline.

items.title: The full picture of loss
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. We work on contingency, with no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on SR-120 near Manteca. Is a wrongful death claim different from the criminal case?
items.answer: Yes. A wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by the family, while any criminal charges are pursued by the state. The two proceed on separate tracks, and a civil claim can move forward whether or not charges are filed. We can explain how the police report from San Joaquin County fits into your claim.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The law gives first priority to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children. If none of those relatives exist, certain financially dependent family members or heirs may be able to file instead. Standing rules can get complicated in blended families, so it is worth having an attorney review your specific situation.

items.question: How long do we have to act, and what does it cost to find out?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit, but claims involving a government entity require a formal notice much sooner. Contact us for a free case review. We work on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery.
